source.title: Viral Proteins Reveal Geometry of Protein Language Models
source.authors: A. Bigot; Harmon Bhasin; C. Park; E. Shakhnovich; Dian-Zhuo Wang

record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-related measurements to protein language models and different training objectives, reporting reconstruction-perplexity and downstream classification results across model scales.
record.gate_note: The paper does not fit power laws to held-out pretraining loss, measure training tokens or compute, or test compute-optimal allocation or fixed-parameter architecture effects. Its own protein-perplexity and held-out viral-classification results across scales bear on V5 and V6. Scaling-law statements cited from other work are not results from this study. PCA correlations, synthetic-sequence comparisons, and cited downstream findings are not separate rows for the tested versions.
record.test_reason: The paper studies how viral proteins sit in protein-LM embedding space. It never fits a power law to held-out loss or varies tokens or compute. It has no fixed-compute, fixed-parameter or fit-method comparison. Its scale comparisons use thresholded fractions and perplexity medians, with only 2-6 sizes per family. These are a different construct from V5's power-law form in other modalities. The viral/cellular classification AUCs are a probe task with no relation to pretraining loss, so they are not V6's downstream predictability. The paper cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only as background.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Scaling contracts viral displacement unevenly across families, and the family ranking depends on the training objective. Embeddings keep viral-specific signal beyond perplexity and shallow features. The record treats this as a test of V5 and V6, but the authors make no scaling-law claim; they cite Kaplan and Hoffmann only as background.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes protein-model embeddings, masked-reconstruction or model-native perplexity, family nativization, and viral classification; it does not reproduce the language-model loss-scaling fits or compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Per-family response differs across scale; the family ranking differs by model objective. Perplexity thresholds are objective-specific, and the paper cautions against comparing their absolute values across architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Protein-model scale (ESMC, ProGen2, EvoDiff) lowers masked or causal perplexity unevenly across viral families. Some families are nativized, some stay displaced, and the viral-cellular gap widens for EvoDiff.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling protein language models reduces perplexity on underrepresented groups unevenly across groups.

fits_no_version.finding: Embedding-probe AUC for viral vs cellular classification rises with scale (ProGen2 0.975 to 0.993, EvoDiff 0.965 to 0.986). Perplexity-only AUC is non-monotonic or falls with scale (ProGen2 0.82 to 0.72).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear probes on pLM embeddings separate viral from cellular proteins better than perplexity does, and the gap grows with scale.

record.problems: The study does not fit power laws to held-out pretraining loss or test tokens/compute; the EvoDiff scale comparison has only two sizes; several per-family ESM results are available only as plots or qualitative descriptions; human-only negative classification uses a small held-out pool (n=38), as the authors note.
record.rows_left_out: No other results directly bearing on V5 or V6 were omitted. PCA/PPL correlations, sequence controls, and detailed low-FPR operating points were not extracted as separate rows because they do not measure the specific scaling-law or downstream-AUC outcomes recorded here.

untested.parts: All of it: no power-law fits of loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
All of it: no extrapolation from small runs.
All of it: no compute-optimal allocation.
All of it: no fixed-parameter architecture comparison.
No power-law fit for protein models, and no test of image/video, repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer regimes.
No test of downstream task performance against scale or pretraining loss; the only task is viral/cellular classification.
No comparison of exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tests/T3 call and its V5 limits_scope and V6 supports/limits_scope labels are withdrawn. The rows measure thresholded family fractions and probe AUCs, which are different constructs from V5 and V6. The study has no pretraining-loss power-law fits or comparisons, so it is T6 with no version verdicts. All 20 rows move to no version. The 'reversed' state on r16 and the 'partial' states on r15, r19 and r20 only describe a perplexity-classifier artefact.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law fits and bottleneck conditions.
No small-run power-law fits or predictions of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute budget comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.

The study evaluates protein-model reconstruction scores and related scaling patterns, but does not fit or compare power-law forms for held-out pretraining loss; it does not test image/video models, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer as scaling regimes.
Tests viral-versus-cellular classification on held-out data, not a broad set of downstream tasks or a general relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss.

No comparison of fitted exponents, parameter-counting conventions, fitting methods, or training schedules. Objective-dependent family rankings are reported, but not as a test of fitted scaling-law dependence.

rows.subject: ESMC
rows.operation_detail: Compared the fraction of human viral proteins with masked-reconstruction PPL < 5 across model sizes.
rows.measure: Fraction of sequences below the native-like PPL threshold
rows.note: The study describes the overall increase as slight; this thresholded fraction is not a fitted held-out loss curve.
rows.check: Fraction of viral proteins under a fixed PPL<5 cutoff is not a power-law fit to held-out loss, so it does not measure V5. The text calls the average rise slight (~5% to ~17%).

rows.subject: ESMC
rows.operation_detail: Compared the fraction of sequences below PPL < 5 separately across human viral families.

conditions.value: Papillomaviridae and Retroviridae gain roughly 60%; Orthomyxoviridae, Orthoherpesviridae, and Sedoreoviridae remain mostly outside the native-like region at 6B

rows.note: The text explicitly describes heterogeneous family responses; exact family-specific plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Per-family fractions are figure-only and describe heterogeneity across viral families, not a scaling-law form.

rows.subject: ESM2 and ESM3
rows.size_stated: ESM2: 8M to 15B; ESM3: SMALL to LARGE
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the per-family nativization analysis across ESM2 and ESM3 sizes.
rows.measure: Per-family nativization rate across model sizes
rows.value: The paper states that Papillomaviridae and Retroviridae also rise under ESM2 and ESM3 scaling.
rows.note: Qualitative cross-family scaling result; the text gives no specific rates for these models.
rows.check: Qualitative statement about families rising under ESM2/ESM3 scaling, with no numbers and no law form.

rows.subject: ProGen2
rows.operation_detail: Compared the fraction of viral sequences below a fixed, model-family-specific native-like threshold across four sizes.
rows.measure: Fraction of viral sequences below τ
rows.note: The threshold is defined as the 90th percentile of cellular perplexity at the reference scale; this is not a power-law fit to held-out pretraining loss.
rows.check: The threshold fraction depends on an arbitrary 90th-percentile cutoff; it is not a loss-vs-scale law.

rows.subject: ProGen2
rows.operation_detail: Compared cellular median perplexity across scale.
rows.note: Two endpoint values are reported; no loss-law fit is provided.
rows.check: Only two endpoint values for cellular median PPL over 4 sizes. Cellular PPL falls substantially (6.5 to 2.7), but without a fit this cannot show a power law.

rows.subject: ProGen2
rows.operation_detail: Compared family-specific viral perplexity and nativization across scale.
rows.measure: Median PPL and fraction below τ
rows.baseline: Median PPL 17.8 and 13% below τ at 151M
rows.value: Median PPL 1.8 and 82% below τ at 6.4B
rows.note: The paper identifies this family as one of ProGen2's strongest nativizers.
rows.check: Family-level nativization fraction, not a loss scaling form.

rows.subject: ProGen2
rows.operation_detail: Compared family-specific nativization across scale.
rows.note: Exact values are stated for the two endpoints.
rows.check: Family-level nativization fraction, not a loss scaling form.

rows.subject: ProGen2
rows.operation_detail: Compared family-specific nativization across scale.
rows.note: The paper says this family nativizes under both ESMC and ProGen2.
rows.check: Family-level nativization fraction, not a loss scaling form.

rows.subject: ProGen2
rows.operation_detail: Compared family-specific perplexity changes across scale.
rows.value: Median perplexities do not decrease with scale; ΔPPL between +0.4 and +1.3
rows.note: The range is reported jointly for these families, without assigning individual values.
rows.check: Family-level PPL change; it does not test the V5 power-law form.

rows.subject: EvoDiff OA-DM
rows.operation_detail: Compared cellular and viral-family median perplexities across the two available scales.
rows.note: Only two scales are available; the authors call this a direction-of-effect result, not a full scaling law.
rows.check: Two sizes only; the authors call it a direction-of-effect result, not a scaling law.

rows.subject: EvoDiff OA-DM
rows.operation_detail: Compared viral-family median perplexities across the two available scales.
rows.value: Per-family changes between −0.1 and −0.7; the viral–cellular gap widens
rows.note: The text reports a range across families rather than family-specific assignments.
rows.check: Two sizes only; family-level PPL changes, not a scaling law.

rows.subject: ESM pLMs
rows.size_stated: 13 ESM probes spanning ESM2, ESMC, and ESM3 scales
rows.stage_stated: pretrained representations with trained logistic-regression probes
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated held-out human viral-versus-cellular classification using linear probes on mean-pooled embeddings.

conditions.value: homology-controlled held-out human viral/cellular test split

rows.uncertainty: 95% percentile bootstrap confidence intervals over 2,000 resamples are shown in Figure 7; exact interval values not stated
rows.note: The paper states that probes exceed shallow-feature baselines at every ESM scale and reach the 0.97–1.00 band for larger models.
rows.check: Viral-vs-cellular AUC for linear probes is a different task and construct from V6. It is not plotted against pretraining loss, and pretraining loss and scale are not related by any fit.

rows.note: The paper reports this as the smallest-scale ProGen2 embedding-probe result.
rows.check: Probe AUC on one specific classification task; not downstream performance versus loss.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Protein-model reconstruction and nativization results across ESM, ProGen2, and EvoDiff scales
reader_labels.reason: Scaling responses vary by viral family and objective; some families change substantially while others remain displaced or nearly flat, and EvoDiff's viral–cellular gap widens. The paper does not fit power laws to held-out pretraining loss. Rows r1–r11.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Embedding-probe viral/cellular classification for ESM, ProGen2, and EvoDiff
reader_labels.reason: Held-out probe AUCs are high and, for ProGen2 and EvoDiff, increase from the smallest to largest reported scale; ESM probes exceed the shallow-feature baseline. Rows r12–r14 and r17–r18.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Perplexity-only viral/cellular classification for ProGen2 and EvoDiff
reader_labels.reason: The readout is not consistently improved by scale: ProGen2 AUC falls from 0.82 to 0.72, while EvoDiff rises from 0.78 to 0.88 but remains at or below the shallow-feature baseline. Rows r15–r16 and r19–r20.
